what_it_does: Processing-in-memory (doing math inside or next to the memory chip rather than shipping data to a separate processor) is promising for AI workloads, but to get the most out of the hardware you need to carefully decide which computation maps to which memory bank and in what data layout. Previous tools either relied on hand-crafted rules or brute-forced through possibilities, both producing poor or slow results. OptiPIM frames the mapping problem as a precise mathematical optimization (Integer Linear Programming — a technique that finds the best answer within a bounded set of yes/no choices) and solves it automatically in roughly four minutes. It plugs into the standard MLIR compiler infrastructure, so regular PyTorch workloads can flow through it without manual tuning.
